key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation relative to BA spacers under ambient light and thermal stress.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskite nanoflakes under ambient light and thermal stress.
Used confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy to investigate structural degradation.
Used X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to assess chemical changes.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, but PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or device lifetime, so performance–stability trade-offs remain unresolved.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
